Silence one finding with a comment on its line or the line above: `# rusty-ignore: rule_id` (several rule ids can be separated with commas, or use `all`).

sections.heading: Frameworks
sections.text:
Frameworks connect files in ways that imports alone do not show: a route registered to a handler, a service injected into a controller, a component rendered by another. For each framework below, Rusty reads the literal forms from source and project files. Forms built at run time, such as computed paths, are reported as diagnostics instead of being guessed. An adapter runs only for packages that declare the framework.

| Framework | Language | What it reads |
|-----------|----------|---------------|
| React | TypeScript, JavaScript | Components rendered by other components (JSX) |
| Next.js | TypeScript, JavaScript | App Router and Pages Router pages and API routes |
| Angular | TypeScript | Components used in templates, router entries, injected services |
| Vue | TypeScript, JavaScript | Single-file components used in templates, Vue Router entries |
| Express | TypeScript, JavaScript | Routes on `express()` apps and routers |
| NestJS | TypeScript | Controller routes, injected providers |
| Django | Python | URL patterns, models and their tables, management commands |
| Flask | Python | Routes on apps and blueprints |
| FastAPI | Python | Routes on apps and routers, `Depends` providers |
| Spring Boot | Java | Controller routes, injected beans, `@Entity` tables |
| ASP.NET Core | C# | Controller and minimal API routes, registered services, EF Core tables |
| Laravel | PHP | Routes, Eloquent models and their tables, Artisan commands, container bindings |
| Symfony | PHP | Attribute and YAML routes, Doctrine entities, console commands, autowired services |
| Gin | Go | Routes on engines and groups |
| Echo | Go | Routes on instances and groups |
| net/http | Go | `HandleFunc` and `Handle` patterns |
| Axum | Rust | Routes and their handlers |
| Actix Web | Rust | Route attributes and `.route(...)` registrations |
| Tauri | Rust | Commands registered with `generate_handler!` |

Spring Boot relations are read from Java sources only; Kotlin Spring code gets the import graph and code health, but not routes or injection yet.

> [!NOTE]
> A relation is only drawn when the code states it literally. Where a framework works by naming convention (for example a table name derived from a class name), the relation is marked as a convention rather than as declared.

sections.heading: Missing a language or framework?
sections.text: Open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/traian18/rusty-ide/issues) with the language or framework and, if you can, a public repository that uses it.

title: Token optimisations
summary: Configure how Rusty reduces repeated context and command output, and inspect the savings.

sections.text: Rusty can reduce the text sent to a model and keep more of a conversation eligible for provider prompt caching. Open **Settings → Token optimisations** to enable or disable each optimisation. They are enabled by default. Changes apply from the next command.

sections.heading: Available optimisations
sections.text:
| Setting | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| **Condense command output** | Removes routine progress and passing-test output while keeping errors, failures and summaries. Applies to `run_command`, `run_check`, `install_dependencies` and `job_output` progress. |
| **Keep full output recallable** | Keeps condensed command output in memory so the agent can retrieve it with `job_output` rather than rerun the command. The last 30 outputs are held until Rusty quits. |
| **Don't resend what the agent already has** | Replaces identical tool results in the same conversation with a pointer; a changed file can be returned as changed lines instead of another full copy. Separate workflow steps and sub-agents get their own copy. |
| **Limit very large tool reports** | Shortens reporting-tool results over 12,000 characters, retaining the beginning and end and a `job_output` reference to the full text. File reads and spec documents are not cut. |
| **Carry the working set across turns** | Gives the next agent in a chat a short list of files read or changed and searches run, helping it avoid repeating exploration. It lists locations, not file contents. |
| **Cache-friendly chat history** | Moves the history cutoff in steps rather than on every turn, so the prefix is more likely to match the provider's prompt cache. Some additional older messages may be omitted; pinned messages and the opening request remain. |
| **Keep the model on a warm cache** | Avoids switching a cached conversation to a cheaper model mid-run, which would require paying for the conversation again. A step up to a more capable model can still happen. |

A shortened result identifies the saved output when recall is available. Ask the agent to read it back if it needs more detail. Cached output is temporary, not a permanent archive.

sections.heading: Safeguards and measurements
sections.text:
Rusty skips an optimisation if it would not make text smaller or if the optimisation fails. Shortened output is marked so it is not condensed again.

The **What it saved** section shows command-output characters in and out, the percentage saved, and how often retained output was read back. A high read-back rate may mean a filter leaves out useful detail. Prompt-cache statistics are shown there too. These figures are not a guarantee of token or cost savings: tokenisation, provider caching and pricing vary. Use **Reset** to clear the displayed statistics.

[Smart tools](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/smart-tools/) are a separate, opt-in way to use a selector model to return focused excerpts. Their selector calls have their own token costs. See [Observability & metrics](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/observability/) for usage tracking.

title: Troubleshooting
summary: Fixes for startup, sign-in, model, update and storage problems.

sections.heading: The window opens off-screen or at a strange size
sections.text:
At launch, Rusty checks the restored window against the displays that are connected. If the size is unusable or the title bar is unreachable, it opens a default-sized window on an available display instead. Valid window geometry is kept, and fullscreen is never restored automatically.

Window display does not wait for the interface to finish loading, so configuration and workspace startup checks can show their own progress and recovery controls. Recovery diagnostics are written to standard error with the `[startup/window]` prefix, which helps when you report a problem.

If a startup step fails, Rusty shows a banner and retry controls rather than leaving you on a blank screen.

sections.heading: A model does not appear in the picker
sections.text:
- Open **LLM Integrations**, select the provider and fetch its model catalog again.
- Check the **Connection Base URL**. For OpenAI-compatible servers it normally ends in `/v1`, for example `http://localhost:11434/v1` for Ollama.
- If your server lists models somewhere other than `{base URL}/models`, set the **Model Catalog URL**.
- For a custom provider, make sure the model names in **Models** match what the server reports.

sections.heading: An API key seems to be ignored
sections.text:
- A blank key falls back to an environment variable such as `OPENAI_API_KEY`, but apps launched from Finder or the Dock do not see variables exported in your shell profile. Paste the key into the provider's **API Authorization Key** field instead.
- Confirm the **Default API Protocol** and **Authentication** match the service. Anthropic uses **Anthropic Messages** with **Anthropic x-api-key**.
- GitHub Models needs a personal access token with the `models:read` scope.

sections.heading: Claude models are not available
sections.text: Claude models are reached with an **Anthropic API key**, through the Anthropic provider. Signing in with a Claude subscription is not supported.

sections.heading: GitHub Copilot or OpenAI Codex sign-in fails
sections.text:
- The first sign-in downloads that provider's runtime, so you need an internet connection. If the download fails, sign in again to retry.
- Use **Cancel**, then **Sign in** again if a sign-in seems stuck.
- Expand **Authentication diagnostics** and use **Copy Diagnostics** to capture details.
- Available models depend on your subscription and, for Copilot, your organization's policy.

sections.heading: My keys disappeared, or settings will not save
sections.text:
Secrets are encrypted with a key held in the macOS Keychain. See [Data, storage & privacy](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/privacy/#provider-keys-and-mcp-credentials):

- If the Keychain is **locked**, Rusty will not save over your existing configuration during that session. Unlock the Keychain and restart Rusty.
- If the Keychain entry was **reset**, Rusty cannot decrypt the old data. It keeps the old data aside and starts fresh, and **Settings → System → Storage & Cache** tells you to re-enter your tokens.

sections.heading: A command was denied and the agent is stuck
sections.text: If you chose **Deny**, the agent is told and should try another approach. If it keeps retrying the same command, stop the run and rephrase the request, or add a [`deny` rule with a clear reason](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/permissions/#rules) to the profile so it knows what to do instead.

sections.heading: Auto does not appear, or a workflow does not switch
sections.text: The **Auto** entry needs OpenRouter and a JEV decision model, and flow switching needs its checkbox on and a workflow that lists where it may hand over to. See [Troubleshooting Auto flows](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/auto-flows/#troubleshooting).

sections.heading: A stage did not use the last result
sections.text: A stage builds on the last result in the same chat. A new chat starts clean, and a workflow of your own reads the last result only if one of its steps binds `/context`. See [Steer a long job between stages](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/workflows/#steer-a-long-job-between-stages).

sections.heading: A build step could not run a check
sections.text: Build changes the code first, then tries to run the project's checks. A command that fails is read, not given up on: Build tries an installed alternative, another download URL or a web search for the error. If a check still cannot run, the result says which command failed with its output, and ends with the command for you to run and what to report back. Run it in a terminal and paste the output into the chat; the next stage continues from there. A common cause is a build wrapper (such as `./mvnw`) that cannot download its tool: running it once in a terminal, or installing the tool, fixes it for every later run.

sections.heading: An update will not install
sections.text:
- Check under **Settings → System → Software Update**.
- If you installed with Homebrew, run `brew upgrade --cask rusty-ide`.
- Otherwise download the latest DMG from the [download page](https://rusty-edit.dev/download/) and replace the app in Applications.

sections.heading: Rusty is using a lot of disk space
sections.text: Open **Settings → System → Storage & Cache** and use **Delete Cache**. It clears the WebView cache, process logs and local execution telemetry without touching your workspaces, project files or settings.

sections.heading: Still stuck?
sections.text: Open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/traian18/rusty-ide/issues) and include your macOS version, the Rusty version (from **Settings → System**) and any diagnostics you copied.

title: The workflow editor
summary: A reference for every switch, menu and field in the Behaviors tab and the Agent Mode workflow bar.

sections.text:
Workflows are edited in the **Behaviors** tab and run from the **workflow bar** in Agent Mode. This page lists every control in both, in the order you meet them. To learn by doing, follow [Your first workflow](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/first-workflow/). For the JSON files behind the editor, see [Profiles & workflows](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/behaviors/).

> [!NOTE]
> A **workflow** is a graph of steps. A **profile** says what one agent step may do: its instructions, tools, limits, rules and completion checks. A workflow step names a profile. The two live side by side in the editor and are saved as `.rusty/workflows/<id>.json` and `.rusty/profiles/<id>.json`.

sections.heading: The workflow bar in Agent Mode
sections.text:
The bar sits above the message box. It decides what the chat follows and shows a run's progress.

| Control | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| **Mode** menu | Chooses what the chat follows. **Single agent** is one loop that decides its own path. **Auto** lets Rusty choose for each message. Every other entry is a workflow, labelled **Stage:** (a short run that stops at a written result) or **Workflow:** (a whole job). Your own workflows are listed here too. |
| **Auto** entry | Appears only when OpenRouter and a decision model are connected. Otherwise a chat that already used it shows *Auto (needs OpenRouter and a JEV model)*. See [Auto flows](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/auto-flows/). |
| Name chip, **×** | Shows the workflow the chat follows. The **×** (*Stop following this workflow*) returns the chat to **Single agent**. It disappears while a run is going. |
| Step list | The steps in the order they run, with each one's state: *not run*, **running**, **waiting for permission**, **waiting for your answer**, **retrying**, **done** or **failed**. A **×2** beside a step means its second attempt. Hover a step for its message. |
| Summary text | While running, for example *Running step 2 of 4: Build*, with *(waiting for permission)*, *(waiting for your answer)* or *(attempt 2)* when it applies. |
| **Allow flow switching** | A checkbox, shown when the chat follows a workflow or Auto. When on, Rusty checks after each step whether what it found means another workflow is the right one, and hands over with the work so far. It does not ask first; when the new workflow can change files, the chat says so. It is greyed while a run is going. See [Auto flows](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/auto-flows/#hand-over-mid-run). |
| **Auto mode** | A checkbox, always shown and never greyed. When on, nothing waits for you: approval steps (including those marked **Always ask a person**) are approved, a stuck task is tried once more and then skipped, and commands and questions are answered for you. It applies to every chat at once and is remembered. See [Auto mode](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/agent-mode/#auto-mode). |
| No-activity notice | Appears after a minute without any sign of life from the running step, with how long it has been quiet and **Stop workflow**. When the workflow has a stall timeout, it also says when the step will be cancelled and retried. Waiting for your permission or your answer does not count. |
| Chevron | Hides or shows the bar. Hidden, it keeps a one-line summary. Rusty remembers your choice. |

### The approval card

When a step needs you, a card opens between the bar and the message box, headed *<step> needs your answer*. It shows the step's question, the result to review (rendered as Markdown; a list such as the manual checks reads as one block per item), a **Notes** box and the step's buttons. *The workflow waits for your answer.*

| Card | Buttons |
|------|---------|
| An **approval step**, such as **Plan approval** or **Manual checks** | **Approve**, **Request changes** (needs notes; offered until the step's change limit is reached) and **Reject**. |
| A **stuck task** in a task queue | **Try again**, **Skip this task**, **Revise the plan** (needs notes; offered when an agent step wrote the plan) and **Stop**. |

Your answer is logged in the chat, for example *Your answer to Plan approval: approve (use the existing helper)*. What each button does is described in [How workflows work](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/how-workflows-work/#approval).

While a run is going the **Mode** menu is locked. While a chat follows a workflow, the **skill** menu stays on **build** and reads *tools set per step*; see [What each step can do](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/workflows/#what-each-step-can-do).

sections.heading: The Behaviors tab
sections.text:
Open **Behaviors** in the left rail. It has a toolbar, a list on the left, a canvas in the middle and an inspector on the right. Edits are validated as you make them, and nothing is written to disk until you save.

### Toolbar

| Control | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| **Workflows** / **Profiles** | The switch at the top left. It changes what the list, the canvas and the buttons mean. |
| Breadcrumb | Where you are. When you open a step's profile, it reads *workflow › step › profile*, and clicking the workflow or step returns you. |
| **Run in Agent Mode** | Workflows view only. Saves the workflow if needed, selects it in Agent Mode and opens the chat; your next message there runs it with that chat's model and tools. If the workflow has a blocking problem it says so and does not run. |
| **New workflow** / **New profile** | Asks for an **Id** and creates a file. Ids use lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, must be unused, and cannot start with `rusty.` (reserved). The new file is saved when you save. |
| **Save N** / **Saved** | Writes every changed file. It reads **Saved** and is disabled when nothing is unsaved. <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd> does the same. Rusty saves with a note if validation found problems. New agent sessions in the workspace pick the changes up. |

**New workflow** depends on what is selected. With a **built-in** workflow selected, it makes an independent copy of it, with revision 1 and the id as its name. With one of **your own** selected, or nothing, it starts from a small blank flow: **Input → Execute → Verify → Output**, where Execute and Verify are both agent steps and Verify is told not to edit files.

### The list

In **Workflows**, the list shows the 15 built-ins (tagged **Built-in**) followed by your own. In **Profiles**, it shows **Workspace profiles** first and the **Built-in** profiles after.

| Mark | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| Dot | The file has unsaved changes. |
| Red dot | The file has a validation problem. Hover for the reason. |
| **Built-in** | Read-only, shipped with Rusty, available in every project. |
| **default** | The profile new sessions run under. |

If a file in `.rusty/` cannot be read, a warning under the list names it.

### The workflow canvas

Each step is a node and each connection an edge. Steps show the state of their latest run, and a badge above the canvas summarizes it: *Running in Agent Mode…*, *Last run completed*, *Last run failed* or *Last run cancelled*.

| Control | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| **Input**, **Agent**, **Verify**, **Approval**, **Subflow**, **Output** | Add a step of that kind. Its id is the kind (`approval`, then `approval_2`, …). Disabled on a built-in workflow. |
| Drag a step | Moves it. Positions are saved in the file but ignored by the engine. |
| Drag from a step's right handle to another step | Connects them with a *succeeds* edge. |
| Click a step or an edge | Selects it and shows its settings in the inspector. |
| Double-click an agent step | Opens its profile. |
| Click the empty canvas | Selects the workflow itself. |
| **Open** *profile* (in a step's inspector) | Drills into that step's profile. |

Loops are drawn as dotted lines below the cards: a **Verify** step with a retry target draws a **retry** line back to that step, and an **Approval** step draws a **changes** line back to where requested changes go. Nested loops run in separate lanes so they never cross. An edge that fires on failure is red, dashed and labelled **on failure**.

Each card summarizes its step: its kind and id; for an agent step its tools, the start of its instructions and its profile; for a verify step its number of checks and the step it retries; for an approval step the step it reviews, where changes go, whether auto-approve is allowed, and *revise first* when notes revise the result; for a subflow the workflow it runs, or *a step* and that step's instructions.

When you connect two steps and the second step's **Response format** is **Text / Markdown**, Rusty also passes the first step's final message to it. Deleting the edge takes that back.

### The inspector

At the top: the selection's name, and three buttons. **Edit as JSON** (**Show form** to go back) swaps the form for the raw document. **Revert unsaved changes** undoes your edits since the last save. **Delete file** removes the file from disk after a confirmation. For a built-in, only the JSON toggle is available and the form is read-only, with **Customize a copy** at the top. Drag the divider between the canvas and the inspector to resize it.

sections.heading: Workflow settings
sections.text:
Select nothing on the canvas to edit the workflow itself.

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| **Name** and **Description** | How the workflow is listed. The description is what you read when you hover the Mode menu's summary. |
| **Revision** | A number you bump as you change it. |
| **Status** | **Draft**, **Published** or **Deprecated**. |
| **Optional limits** | Budgets for the whole run. Leave a field empty for no limit. |
| **Advanced data contracts** | **Output contract** (optional: by default the result is the text of the **Output** step; set it only to check the result against a schema) and **Input schema**, as JSON. Rarely needed. |

The limits are **Steps**, **Total attempts**, **Duration (seconds)**, **Stall timeout (seconds)**, **Model requests**, **Tool calls**, **Tokens** and **Cost (USD)**. The stall timeout cancels and retries a step that shows no sign of life for that long; time spent waiting for your permission or answer does not count. The built-in workflows set **Total attempts** to 40 and **Stall timeout** to 600 seconds. You can stop a running workflow at any time regardless. See [Limits](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/how-workflows-work/#limits).

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text:
Select a step to edit it. Every step has a **Name** and a read-only **Id**, and at the bottom:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| **Attempts** | How many times the step may run, 1 to 10. One by default; raise it to allow retries after a failure such as a rate limit, and on any step a Verify step sends work back to. Which failures may use the attempts is the step's `retry_on` list, set with **Edit as JSON**; a retry target must list `verification_failed`. |
| **Timeout (seconds)** | Stops the step after this long. Empty means no limit. |
| **Advanced data mapping** | **Input bindings** and **Output schema** as JSON, for data a form cannot express. |
| **Delete step** | Removes the step and every edge touching it. |

### Agent steps

The step that does the work.

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| **Profile** | How the step's agent behaves. **Session default** means no profile: the chat's own settings apply. A name followed by *(missing)* means the file is gone. |
| **Open** *profile* / **Design a profile for this step** | Opens the profile, or creates a new one named after the step and assigns it. |
| **Instructions** | What this step should do, added to the request. |
| **Run the plan as a task queue** | Builds the plan bound to the step one task at a time: each task in a fresh builder session, checked by a read-only reviewer, and saved once accepted. Ticking it fills in **Task queue and reviewer** (JSON) with the defaults the built-ins use: `plan_pointer` (where the plan is bound, for example `/plan`), `review_profile`, `review_instructions`, `max_repairs` (2) and `on_task_failure` (`ask`; also `skip` or `stop`). An optional `flows` map names workflows a planned task may run instead of a builder. Four built-in pipelines use it. See [Task queues](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/how-workflows-work/#task-queues). |
| **Context from earlier steps** | Text steps only. Tick the **Original request** and any earlier step whose final message this step should receive. |
| **Tools** | **Everything the session has**, **Only these tools** (with a searchable checklist) or **No tools**. |
| **Context** | **Isolated**: a fresh session that inherits your workspace, model and permissions. Keep it on **Isolated**: the **Shared session** option is listed, but the engine does not support it yet and a step set to it fails. |
| **Model** | A model for this step, or empty for the session's. With [automatic model selection](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/auto-model-selection/) on, an empty field lets Rusty rate the step. |
| **Response format** | **Text / Markdown** passes the final message straight to the next step. **Require the provider's structured output**, **Provider's, else host validation** and **JSON with host validation** return a checked JSON result, shaped by the step's **Output schema**, that a Verify step can test. **JSON with host validation** is the one that works with every provider; the model answers in Markdown sections and Rusty reads them into the schema. Changing the format resets the output schema. |

### Verify steps

A check on an earlier step's result.

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| **Checks** | A JSON list. `{"type": "criteria", "pointer": "/check/criteria"}` judges a list of `{id, status, evidence}` criterion by criterion: `fail` sends the work back, `manual` moves on and is listed for an approval step; add `"plan_pointer": "/plan"` to require every criterion of a bound plan. `{"type": "schema"}` checks the shape. `{"type": "required_status", "pointer": "/status", "equals": "done"}` requires a field to have a value. `{"type": "artifact_exists", "pointer": "/path"}` requires a field to be present and not empty, and `artifacts_resolvable` checks that listed files really exist. A check reads what is bound to the step, so set **Input bindings** under **Advanced data mapping**. |
| **On failure, retry** | Choose a step to re-run, with the failure as feedback, or **Nothing (follow on_failure edges)**. Set it, and give the retried step more **Attempts** and `verification_failed` in its `retry_on`, to make a loop. The step must be an agent step that runs before this one. |

### Approval steps

A point where the run waits for you. See [Approval](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/how-workflows-work/#approval) for what each answer does.

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| **Review the result of** | The earlier step whose result the card shows. A new approval step starts on the latest agent step. |
| **Question** | Shown above the result. Empty uses *Review <step> before the workflow continues.* |
| **Requested changes go to** | **The step being reviewed**, or another agent step that runs earlier. That step runs again with your notes, and so does every step in between. |
| **Times changes may be asked for** | 0 to 10, 5 by default. After that, the card offers only **Approve** and **Reject**. |
| **Skip when empty at** | A JSON pointer into what is reviewed. When nothing is there (missing, empty text, empty list), the step passes without asking. Empty means never skip. |
| **Always ask a person, even when the run auto-approves** | The run does not pass the step by itself. **Auto mode** still approves it, since in auto mode nobody is asked. |
| **Notes given with an approval revise the result first** | **Approve** with notes sends the notes back like **Request changes**, and once the result is revised the approval stands without asking again. Off, notes are only recorded in the approval's result. |

### Subflow steps

Runs another workflow, or one extra step, inside this one. See [Subflow](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/how-workflows-work/#subflow).

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| **Run** | **A single step** or **A saved workflow**. |
| **Workflow** | For a saved workflow: any workflow in the list except this one, including the built-in ones under their full ids (`rusty-ide.builtin.…`). A name followed by *(not found)* no longer exists. |
| **Profile** and **Instructions** | For a single step: the profile it runs under and what it should do. |

Whatever is bound to the step (**Advanced data mapping**, **Input bindings**) is the child run's whole input; the built-in workflows read `request` and `context`, so bind both. The child's result is this step's result.

### Input and Output steps

**Input** receives the run input: `request`, `context` and `attachments`. **Input defaults** supplies values for fields the run input does not carry; they reach steps that read the Input step's result, not steps that read the run input directly. **Output** picks the result: **Show the final message from** a step. **Advanced source mapping** sets it as JSON, for example with `"pointer": "/summary"` to show one field of a structured result.

### Edges

**Follow when the source step** is **succeeds** for the normal path or **fails** to route a failure somewhere else. A step has exactly one **succeeds** edge (except an Output step, which has none) and at most one **fails** edge, and edges cannot form a cycle: use a Verify step's retry target or an Approval step for loops. **Delete edge** removes it. Deleting a **succeeds** edge into a Text / Markdown agent step also removes the input that connecting it added.

sections.heading: Profiles
sections.text:
Switch to **Profiles**. The canvas shows each profile as a node, with `switch_profile` rules drawn as edges. Drag from one profile's right handle to another to add a rule that switches to it after three turns, then click the edge to edit that rule. Built-in profiles are read-only, so connect from one of yours.

### Profile settings

| Section | Fields |
|---------|--------|
| **Profile** | **Name**, **Description**, **Revision**, **Status**. Sessions load published profiles by default; a workflow run also uses drafts. **Make workspace default** makes new sessions run under this profile (**Workspace default ✓** when it is). |
| **Instructions** | **Mode**: **Append to the system prompt** or **Replace the system prompt**. **Text**. |
| **Tools** | **Available tools**: **Everything the session has**, **Only these tools** or **No tools**. Under **Per-tool settings**, choose a tool to set its **Permission** (**Session default**, **Allow if session permits**, **Ask before running**, **Deny**) and **Extra instructions** the model reads about that tool. |
| **Model and limits** | **Model**, **Reasoning effort** (**Low**, **Medium**, **High**), **Max turns**, **Max tool calls**, and **Final turn prompt**, sent on the last allowed turn. |
| **Rules** | See below. |
| **Completion gate** | See below. |
| **Child agents** | Subagents inherit this profile. Other policies are not supported by the current engine and are kept untouched if a file has one. |

A profile that allows only some tools can never use the rest. The checklist also lists tools that follow another: **Edit Part of a File** follows **Write Files**, and **Run Project Checks** and **Install Dependencies** follow **Run Commands**. Anything written for the main tool applies to the follower, so a read-only profile stays read-only. See [Profiles & workflows](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/behaviors/#profile-fields).

### Rules

A rule reacts to an event with an action. Rules are grouped by the event they run on. Pick an event and an action next to **Add rule**, then click it, and open the new rule to edit it.

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| **Rule id** | A name for the rule. |
| **Runs on** | The event: `RunStart` (once), `BeforeModelRequest` (every request), `PreToolUse` (before a tool runs), `PostToolUse` (after it succeeds), `PostToolUseFailure` (after it fails), `ProfileEntered` (when a switch lands here). |
| **Action** | `inject` adds text to the model's context. `deny` blocks a tool call with a reason the model sees. `ask` asks you first. `allow` runs it without asking. `stop_run` ends the run with a reason. `switch_profile` hands over to another profile. `rewrite_args` changes a call's arguments. `rewrite_result` appends to or replaces a tool's result. A menu entry reads *(not for …)* when the action does not fit the event. |
| **Max fires** | The most times the rule may trigger. Empty is unlimited. |
| **When this rule applies** | An optional condition. See below. |

**Conditions** narrow when a rule or check applies:

| Condition | True when |
|-----------|-----------|
| **Tool matches** | The tool is one you tick. |
| **Tool argument matches** | An argument, found by its path such as `/path`, matches a pattern, contains text or equals a value. |
| **Tool result contains text** | The result includes the text. |
| **Turn number** | The turn count is exactly, at least or at most a number. |
| **Tool call count** | The chosen tools have been called that many times. |
| **Turns since a tool ran** | That many turns have passed since the chosen tools last ran. |
| **Tools run after another tool** | After the first tools ran, the second tools ran afterwards. |
| **A tool is available to the agent** | The tool was offered on the latest request. |
| **Repeated identical calls** | The same call happened that many times. |
| **Previous profile** | The run arrived from one of the profiles you tick. |
| **All conditions**, **Any condition**, **Condition is not met** | Combine other conditions. |

The counting conditions can be limited to calls that **Ran (any result)**, **Succeeded**, or **Failed**.

### Completion gate

Checks that run when the model says it is done. A failed check sends its **Feedback** back and the agent keeps working, up to **Additional attempts**. **If checks still fail** is **Fail the run** or **Finish with checks not passed**.

Each check has a **Check name**, a method, and **Feedback when this check fails**:

| Method | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| **Check tool activity** | Passes when a condition holds, such as *Tool call count* of **Read Files** at least 1. |
| **Run a tool** | Runs a tool you choose with arguments you set. |
| **Ask a model** | A model reads recent messages against your **Review instructions**. |
| **Ask a reviewer agent** | A reviewer agent with its own tools and **Reviewer turn limit** inspects the work. |
| **Run a command** | Runs a command. Only when the session trusts profile commands. |

For the model, agent and command methods, **If the reviewer errors** chooses whether an error counts as a failure or a pass. **Add check**, **Remove check** and **Remove completion gate** edit the list.

sections.heading: Tips
sections.text:
- Click **Edit as JSON** when the form has no field for what you need. Fields the form does not know are kept when you save.
- Bump **Revision** when you change a file you have already run, so you can tell versions apart.
- Keep **Feedback** specific. It is the message the agent acts on.
- Do not rely on an instruction alone to keep a step from writing. Give it a profile whose tool list leaves out **Write Files**.

title: Workflows
summary: What workflows are, how to run one, what to do when it asks for your approval, and how to steer a long job between stages.

sections.text:
A single agent loop decides its own path: it reads, edits, runs and answers in whatever order it chooses. A **workflow** decides the path for the agent. It says which steps run, in what order, what each step may use, and what must be checked before it can finish.

Rusty ships **20 workflows**, available in every project, from a two-step investigation to a full audit, fix and re-audit. You pick one from the **Mode** menu in [Agent Mode](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/agent-mode/), or let Rusty [choose for you](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/auto-flows/).

This page is about using workflows. For what happens inside a run (steps, handoffs, checks that send work back, approvals, limits), see [How workflows work](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/how-workflows-work/).

| | Single agent | Workflow |
|---|---|---|
| **Path** | The agent decides. | The workflow decides. |
| **Tools** | Whatever the chat's skill allows. | Each step has its own: a planning step cannot edit files at all. |
| **Context** | One long conversation. | Each step starts fresh and receives the previous step's written handoff. |
| **Checks** | Up to the agent. | Build must run the project's checks before it reports, and an independent Verify step checks every acceptance criterion. A failed criterion sends the work back to Build. |
| **You decide** | Whenever you reply. | At set points: you approve the plan before anything is built, and you try the checks only a person can do. |
| **Best for** | Quick questions and small edits. | Work you want broken into steps you can follow, and review. |

sections.heading: Run a workflow
sections.text:
1. Open **Agent Mode**.
2. In the workflow bar above the message box, open the **Mode** menu and choose a workflow. Stages are labelled **Stage:**, pipelines **Workflow:**. Hover the summary line to read what the selected one is for.
3. Describe what you want and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.

While it runs, the bar lists the steps in order and tells you where it is, for example *Running step 4 of 8: Build*. Each step shows its state:

| State | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| *not run* | The step has not started yet. |
| **running** | The step is working. A small **×2** means its second attempt. |
| **waiting for permission** | A command or tool is waiting for you to allow it. |
| **waiting for your answer** | An approval card is open above the message box. See [When a workflow asks you](#when-a-workflow-asks-you). |
| **retrying** | The step will run again: after an error, or because a later step sent the work back. |
| **done** | The step finished. |
| **failed** | The step failed. Hover it for the reason. |

Each agent step runs in a fresh, isolated session that inherits your workspace, your model and your permission policies, and the chat marks where each step's output begins.

Every step starts by writing its own plan, as the agent does in a normal chat, and the **Plan** panel on the right shows it as *Write spec plan 2/5*. Earlier steps' plans fold above the current one; click one to see what it did. A retry, or the next task of a task queue, gets its own list, such as *Build (2)*. A step cannot finish until it has made a plan and closed every item in it, by marking each one done or cancelled. The chat also logs what the engine does between steps, such as *Acceptance sent the work back; running Build again (attempt 2).*

The workflow's final message is its **result**, so read it. A finished run means every step finished, not that every check passed. In the built-in pipelines the result is Verify's summary: what was built, the outcome for each requirement, what you still need to check by hand, and follow-ups.

If a step fails, the bar says so and your next message resumes at the failed step. Steps that already finished are kept. Choose **Start over instead** to discard them.

### Long runs

A step that is busy with a long command or a slow model can be quiet for a while. After a minute without activity the bar says how long it has been quiet and offers **Stop workflow**. The built-in workflows cancel and retry a step that shows no sign of life for 10 minutes; time spent waiting for your permission or your answer does not count. Press **Stop** at any time to end the run.

sections.heading: When a workflow asks you
sections.text:
Some steps wait for you. The run pauses, the bar says *waiting for your answer*, and a card opens above the message box with a question, the result to review, a **Notes** box and buttons. The workflow waits until you answer, however long that takes.

### Approve the plan

Every built-in workflow that changes files shows you its plan before anything is built. The plan lists the requirements, their numbered acceptance criteria, the tasks, how each criterion will be checked, and the decisions and risks you should confirm.

| You choose | What happens |
|------------|--------------|
| **Approve** | Building starts. |
| Notes, then **Approve** | Plan revises the plan to include your notes, then building starts without asking you again. Use it for small corrections such as "use the existing retry helper" or "skip the migration". |
| Notes, then **Request changes** | Plan revises the plan with your notes and shows it to you again. Use it when you want to see the result first. |
| **Reject** | The run ends. Nothing has been changed. |

Build, Verify and any final review all work from the plan as you approved it, and they also see your notes. Where your notes, the plan and your original request disagree, your notes win.

### Try the manual checks

Some things cannot be checked inside the workspace: how a page looks, a flow on a device, a real external service, a command that cannot run on this machine. Verify reports those as **manual**, and once everything else has passed, a **Manual checks** card lists each one with the exact steps to try.

- If they work, choose **Approve**.
- If something does not, describe what you saw in the notes and choose **Request changes**. The work goes back to Build with your description, and Verify checks it again.

When there is nothing to check by hand, the step passes without asking. Pipelines with a final review or a security recheck may ask a second time, for that step's own manual checks.

### Decide about a stuck task

In the pipelines that build one task at a time (see [Task queues](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/how-workflows-work/#task-queues)), a task that still fails its review after its repairs asks what to do: **Try again** (your notes guide the next try), **Skip this task**, **Revise the plan** (your notes go to Plan), or **Stop**. Tasks that were already accepted are kept.

### Auto mode

Tick **Auto mode** in the workflow bar and nothing waits for you: the plan is approved as written, manual checks are approved untried, and a stuck task is tried once more and then skipped (never stopped). Commands and other prompts pass too; see [Auto mode](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/agent-mode/#auto-mode). Steps marked **Always ask a person** are approved as well. Read the result afterwards.

sections.heading: Stages and pipelines
sections.text:
The built-in workflows come in two kinds.

**Stages** are short runs that stop at a written result you can read and amend: findings, a design, a plan, a verdict. Most are two read-only steps. **Build & verify** is the stage that carries a plan out, so it can change files and asks you to approve the plan first.

**Pipelines** run a whole job from start to finish: plan, build, verify, and so on.

Use a pipeline when the path is clear and you want it done. Use stages when you want to look at each result before the next thing happens, when you are not sure yet what to build, or when the change is risky.

See [Built-in workflows](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/built-in-workflows/) for every one, step by step.

sections.heading: Steer a long job between stages
sections.text:
A stage ends with a result in the chat. The next workflow you run **in the same chat** starts from that result: Rusty hands it to the first step as context, and that step builds on it instead of starting over.

That gives you a point to intervene between stages. For example:

1. Run **Stage: Research & analyze** on "how does sync work". Read the findings.
2. Reply with your correction, such as "keep the queue, skip the migration, and design the retry fix", and run **Stage: Architect & plan**. It sees the findings and your correction. Read the plan and edit it in your next message if you want.
3. Run **Stage: Build & verify** to carry the plan out, then **Stage: Verify & review changes** for a second look.

Things to know:

- The context is the **last result in the chat**: the most recent assistant result, leaving out step markers and errors. Very long results are cut at about 24,000 characters.
- Every built-in workflow reads it, so you can start a pipeline after a stage too.
- A **new chat** starts clean. Start one when the next job has nothing to do with the last.
- A single-agent answer counts as a result too, so a stage can build on a quick question you asked first.

sections.heading: Tutorial: audit, then fix what it found
sections.text:
A worked example of the stage-by-stage flow, for a project that needs a security pass.

1. Choose **Stage: Security audit & fix plan** and send "audit the API for authentication and authorization problems". Security inspects the code and ranks its findings (S1, S2, …) by severity; Plan turns them into a fix plan. Nothing is changed. Read the result. Anything only you can do, such as rotating an exposed credential, is listed as a follow-up.
2. Reply with what to include or skip, for example "fix S1 and S3 first; leave the dependency upgrades for later".
3. In the same chat, choose **Stage: Build & verify** and send "go ahead". Its Plan step adopts the fix plan from the chat, applies your reply, and updates only what the code shows is out of date.
4. The **Plan approval** card opens. Check that the plan covers S1 and S3 and leaves the upgrades out. If one detail is wrong, write it in the notes and choose **Approve**: the plan is revised and building starts.
5. Build changes the code and runs the project's checks. Rusty asks before it runs a command, so keep the project open and allow the ones you recognize.
6. Verify checks every acceptance criterion against the workspace. If one fails, the chat says *Acceptance sent the work back*, and Build fixes exactly what failed before Verify checks again.
7. If something can only be checked by a person, for example logging in with a real account, the **Manual checks** card lists the steps. Try them, then approve, or describe what went wrong and choose **Request changes**.
8. Read the result: what was fixed, the outcome for each criterion, and any check you still need to run yourself, with the exact command.

For a bigger job, **Security remediation** does all of this in one run, builds the fixes one at a time, and ends with a security recheck of every original finding.

sections.heading: Keep chatting after a run
sections.text:
A finished workflow does not end the conversation. Your next message in the same chat keeps the context:

- A stage that reads the earlier result gets the last result in the chat as context, as described above.
- A workflow of your own that does not read the context receives your earlier requests and the last result behind your new request, marked as background. A follow-up such as "now fix what you found" does not start from nothing.
- The **Single agent** always sees the whole chat.
- On **Auto**, Rusty reads your message together with what you asked earlier, then picks a workflow or the single agent by itself. It does not ask.

sections.heading: The Result is saved
sections.text:
A workflow that only reads (research, analysis, plans, reviews) saves its Result when it finishes, as a Markdown file in `.rusty/findings/` in your workspace, named by date, time and topic. The file holds the request and the Result, so you can pick the work up later. The chat shows where it went: *Result saved to `.rusty/findings/…`*.

A run that changes files does not save one, because the changes are the outcome. The single agent does not save one either.

sections.heading: What each step can do
sections.text:
Every step runs under a [profile](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/built-in-workflows/#built-in-profiles) that sets its tools. The profiles fall into three kinds:

- **Reads only.** Research, Analyze, Plan, Architect, Security and Review. They read your workspace (and some search the web) but cannot write files or run commands.
- **Runs checks, never edits.** Debug and Verify cannot write files. They may run approved, non-destructive commands to reproduce a failure or check a result.
- **Can change files.** Build, Refactor, Optimize and Document.

While a chat follows a workflow, the **skill** menu stays on **build** and reads *tools set per step*. Each step's profile decides its tools, and a skill such as **plan** would otherwise limit what every step can use. Your own skill choice comes back when you switch to **Single agent**. Permission prompts still apply: commands ask before they run. See [Permissions & safety](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/permissions/).

sections.heading: A model for each step
sections.text: With [automatic model selection](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/auto-model-selection/) on, a workflow does not run on one model. Each step is rated on its own just before it starts, so Research and Verify can run on a light model while Architect runs on a heavy one, in the same run. See [A model for each step](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/auto-model-selection/#workflows-a-model-for-each-step).

sections.heading: Let Rusty choose
sections.text: Choose **Auto** in the Mode menu and Rusty picks the workflow, or the single agent, for each message. It can also hand a running workflow over to another when what a step found changes the plan. Both are covered in [Auto flows](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/auto-flows/).

sections.heading: Make it yours
sections.text:
The built-in workflows are read-only, so they always stay in a known-good state. Choose **Customize a copy** in the Behaviors tab to get an editable version saved in your workspace, or build your own from scratch. Workflows and profiles are plain JSON.

- New to this? Follow [Your first workflow](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/first-workflow/).
- Rather describe it than draw it? The [Workflow Author skill](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/skills/#workflow-author-skill-create-a-workflow-by-describing-it) builds or changes a workflow from a chat.
- Looking for what a control does? See [The workflow editor](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/workflow-editor/).
- Want the files themselves? See [Profiles & workflows](https://rusty-edit.dev/docs/behaviors/).
